   199			\item
   200			      \[
   201				      G_g^{\mathrm A} \ot I \simeq_\nu I \ot G_g^{\mathrm B}.
   202			      \]
   203		\end{enumerate}

   213		boundaries recorded in \cite{gap:issue-906-main-formal-k-bound} and
   214		\cite{gap:issue-422-main-formal-zero-k-boundary}.

   108	\section{The source assertion and the obstruction}
   109	
   110	We examine the final step of the subsection ``Applying the classical
   111	low-degree test'' in the analysis of the Pauli basis test in the compression
   112	paper of Ji, Natarajan, Vidick, Wright, and Yuen (MIP$^{*}$=RE,
   113	arXiv:2001.04383), whose quantum soundness component builds on the low
   114	individual degree test of \cite{Ji2020LowIndividualDegree}.%
   115	\footnote{Tracked in \localissue{0002}.  In the mirror of the source
   116	consulted here, the polynomial-pair lemma and its proof are at
   117	\path{references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex},
   118	lines~1267--1288; the sub-line lemma is at lines~1063--1116 and the combined
   119	line lemma at lines~1020--1034 of the same file.  The game parametrization
   120	with its divisibility, the index function, the soundness statement with its
   121	proof, and admissibility are at
   122	\path{references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex},
   123	lines~33--35, 214--219, 413--458, and 958--961.}
   124	There, the combined point measurements
   125	$\{\hat Q^{x,z,\alpha,\beta}_c\}$ and combined line measurements
   126	$\{\hat Q^{\ell}_f\}$, indexed by points of $\F_q^{2m+2}$ and lines in
   127	$\F_q^{2m+2}$, are asserted to form a strategy for the classical low
   128	individual degree game with parameters
   129	\[
   130	  \mathsf{ldparams} = (q,\, 2m+2,\, d,\, 1)
   131	  \tag{\path{lem:qld-4-7}}
   132	\]
   133	of value $1 - \delta_{\mathrm{combine}}$, and the quantum soundness theorem
   134	for that game is applied to produce the global polynomial-pair measurement.
   135	The two lemmas feeding this step are stated for the line-point distribution
   136	over $\F_q^{2m+2}$.
   137	
   138	The game, however, is parametrized by tuples $(q,m',d,k)$ with $q$ an
   139	admissible field size \emph{and $m'$ dividing $q$}.  The divisibility is not
   140	incidental: the question distribution is a conditionally linear distribution
   141	in which a uniform seed coordinate $s \in \F_q$, read as an integer in
   142	$\{0,\ldots,q-1\}$, determines the axis or diagonal index through the unique
   143	$\chi(s)$ with
   144	\[
   145	  s = (\chi(s)-1)\,\frac{q}{m'} + r, \qquad 0 \le r < \frac{q}{m'},
   146	  \tag{\path{eq:chi-func}}
   147	\]
   148	so that the $m'$ classes $\chi^{-1}(i)$ partition $\F_q$ into sets of equal
   149	size $q/m'$ and the index is uniform.  For $m' \nmid q$ neither the index
   150	function nor the line-point distribution built from it is defined.
   151	
   152	Admissibility of $(q,m,d)$ supplies only $m \mid q$.  Since an admissible $q$
   153	is a power of two, $m \mid q$ forces $m = 2^j$.  For $j \ge 1$ the integer
   154	$m+1 \ge 3$ is odd, so $2m+2 = 2(m+1)$ has an odd factor exceeding $1$ and
   155	divides no power of two; for $m = 1$ the condition $4 \mid q$ holds for every
   156	admissible $q$ except $q = 2$.  Thus the instantiation at dimension $2m+2$ is
   157	undefined for every admissible tuple with $m \ge 2$: for instance
   158	$(q,m,d) = (8,2,1)$ is admissible, while $6 \nmid 8$.  The source performs
   159	the instantiation without addressing the divisibility, so its proof route
   160	establishes the polynomial-pair lemma, and with it the soundness theorem for
   161	the Pauli basis test that rests on it, only for $m = 1$ and $q \ge 8$.

   163	\section{What the cited soundness theorem requires: the import obligations}
   164	\label{sec:import-obligations}
   165	
   166	The quantum soundness theorem for the classical game inherits the constraint
   167	$m' \mid q$ solely because it is stated for the game just described; its
   168	proof fixes an admissible $q$ with $m' \mid q$, asserts that the game with
   169	simultaneity parameter $1$ is \emph{identical} to the two-prover tensor-code
   170	test for the Reed--Solomon tensor code $\mathcal C^{\ot m'}$ of the same
   171	authors' \emph{Quantum soundness of testing tensor codes} (arXiv:2111.08131)
   172	\cite{Ji2021Quantum}, and concludes by Theorem~4.7 there, instantiated with
   173	that theorem's auxiliary integer parameter --- denoted $k$ in that source,
   174	and written $K$ here to avoid clashing with the field exponent and the
   175	simultaneity parameter --- chosen as $(m')^3 d$.  Neither
   176	the asserted identity nor the instantiation is complete as stated, so the
   177	import carries two verification obligations, which this section details and
   178	which the blueprint's proof node for the soundness statement records as
   179	open.  Both obligations are independent of the divisibility question: they
   180	arise at every dimension, for the $\chi$-based game where it is defined and
   181	equally for the directly indexed variant proposed under the candidate
   182	repairs.
   183	
   184	\paragraph{The cited test.}
   185	In the two-prover tensor-code test (Figures~1 and~2 of
   186	\cite{Ji2021Quantum}; the two-prover strategy format and the goodness
   187	measure are Definitions~4.5 and~4.6 there), the referee performs one of
   188	three subtests with probability $1/3$ each, assigning the two roles of each
   189	subtest to the two provers uniformly at random.  \emph{Axis-parallel lines
   190	test}: sample a uniform point $u \in [n]^{m'}$ and a uniform axis
   191	$j \in \{1,\ldots,m'\}$; send the axis-parallel line $\ell$ through $u$ in
   192	direction $j$ to one prover, who answers a codeword $g \in \mathcal C$;
   193	send $u$ to the other, who answers a field value $a$; accept iff
   194	$g(u_j) = a$.  \emph{Subcube commutation test}: sample
   195	$j \in \{1,\ldots,m'\}$ and a subcube $H \subseteq [n]^{m'}$ by fixing the
   196	last $j-1$ coordinates uniformly; sample $u, v$ independently and uniformly

951b7ed docs(QPBT): record the Magic Square rigidity gap
thm:ms-rigidity is false as printed. Its conclusion forces the two
players' Variable_1 and Variable_5 measurements to agree on the shared
state, while the role-symmetric Magic Square game samples only
constraint-variable pairs and never sends the same question to both
players. A perfect strategy that answers the two orientations of each
sampled edge on two independent copies of two EPR pairs violates the
conclusion at eps = 0.

The note also records that the restriction to symmetric strategies
(decision B4 on issue #26) does not repair the statement: the
player-role symmetrization of that strategy, obtained by giving each
player a flag qubit in the state (|01>+|10>)/sqrt2 which selects the
role, is symmetric, has value 1, and has the same vanishing
correlations. The hypothesis that does remove the obstruction is
consistency of the strategy on its state, which is the class the
source's only application supplies.

The note explains why Coladangelo-Stark Theorem 6.9, a self-test for
the one-way linear constraint system game, constrains only one player's
constraint observables and the other player's variable observables, and
therefore does not give the printed conclusion for the role-symmetric
game. Adds the Coladangelo-Stark entry to the paper-gap bibliography and
the note entry to the blueprint bibliography.

|---|---|---|
| `[ ]` | unresolved | **yes** |
| `[x]` | resolved — a human or an agent addressed it and says so | no |
| `[-]` | outdated — the cited lines were rewritten since the reviewed SHA | no |

`[ ]` → `[x]` is a human judgement, or a claim by the fixer that a human is
expected to check; it is never automatic.  There is no automatic `[ ]` → `[-]`
pass: exactly one review is published per head SHA and the merge gate reads only
that one, so a finding written against an older SHA can no longer block and has
nothing to be outdated *out of*.  `[-]` stays available as a hand-written
disposition; a reviewer re-derives its findings from the new diff on every head.

**Merge gate.**  A PR whose current-head review carries any `[ ]` finding is
not mergeable.  The contract for `pr_merge.py` and for humans is exactly the
unchecked-finding regex of `issues-prs.md` §2, `^\s*[-*]\s*\[ \]`, applied to
the marker-bound review body for the head SHA; no match means the ledger is
clean, and the paired `local-review/summary` status must agree.  Anything else
must be resolved, outdated, or adjudicated by the operator under §12 (Round cap
and operator adjudication) — the operator is the adjudicating party; the owner
is consulted only for the escalations named in the standing briefing.  Owner
decision 2026-09-02 (EVOLUTION.md): this supersedes the GitHub-era "never merge
without consulting the user" rule of `docs/pr_review_management.md` for this
repository; the substantive review criteria are unchanged.
A PR that touches only the workflow layer (`local/`, `.githooks/`,
`scripts/tests/`, `docs/`, telemetry) is adjudicated after its SECOND round
because reviewer rounds on scaffolding did not converge (events.md
2026-09-03); a further review is still permitted when the head changed (an
adjudication needs an exact-head review), but it is churn the owner's
watchdog reports.  Mathematics PRs keep the four-round cap above.

Findings do **not** survive across SHAs.  Gate 4 matches the marker
`<!-- mipstarre-review pr=N head=SHA -->` on that exact commit id, so a ledger
written at SHA *A* is invisible at SHA *B* — and a head carrying no review at
all is "not reviewed", never clean.  A finding that still applies is one the
next review re-derives from the new diff.

## 12. Round cap and operator adjudication (2026-08-30)

A PR receives at most **four** full review rounds. From the fifth round on,
the operator may close the loop by adjudication instead of iteration:

1. every remaining finding is either fixed, or converted to a tracked issue;
   the operator posts an **ADJUDICATION comment** on the PR — a body starting
   with `ADJUDICATION`, carrying `head=<final_head>`, and listing the last
   round's findings with every box ticked and a one-line disposition each
   (`fixed in <commit>` / `deferred to issue #NNNN: <reason>` /
   `moot: <reason>`);
2. the comment is the record; nothing local is written;
3. the merge commit names the adjudication and the issues created;
4. `pr_merge.py --adjudicated` accepts it in place of a clean verdict, and
   only for the current head — a stale `head=` is a refusal.

Nothing is dropped silently: an adjudicated finding lives on as an issue.
This mirrors the parent's combined bot-fix iteration cap with a single
terminal review (pr-review.yml:69-72). See EVOLUTION.md for the trigger.

## 13. Evidence follows the diff: carry-forward across a fresh-base (2026-09-04)

The merge gate's fresh-base rule (issues-prs.md, gate 2b) moves a PR's head
every time `main` advances, but a merge of `main` into the branch does not
change the PR's own patch.  `review.sh` therefore compares a whitespace-
sensitive hash of the patch (the diff without its `index`/hunk-header lines,
so hunk positions may move but no byte of content may) with that of every
earlier reviewed head of the same PR whose review is bound to that head and
published by the lane's account; on a match it republishes that head's verdict
and ledger as the exact-head review of the new head, marked "Carried forward
from <sha>" (marker `<!-- mipstarre-review-carried from=<sha> -->`; a carried
review is not a review round and is never itself a carry source), and posts the matching
`local-review/summary` — without dispatching the reviewer.  Adverse verdicts
are carried too, so an adjudication at the new head remains possible.  Any
change to the patch (a repair, a conflict resolution) yields a different
patch-id and a real review.  `--force-review` bypasses the fast path.
status, silent as that is about contexts never posted. The run manifest is one
PR comment marked `<!-- mipstarre-ci-manifest pr=N -->`, kept current by
`ensure-pr-comment`: evidence for humans, while the statuses are the gate.

**Review verdict.** One `COMMENT` review per head SHA, bound to `commit_id`,
carrying `<!-- mipstarre-review pr=N head=SHA -->`, the findings ledger, and the
line `VERDICT: APPROVED | COMMENTED | CHANGES_REQUESTED (code=…, prose=…)`.
Unchecked findings are ledger lines matching `^\s*[-*]\s*\[ \]`; clean means
`APPROVED`, or `COMMENTED` with none of them. Adverse verdicts post as `COMMENT`
too — a **single account** cannot approve its own pull request, so the review
event carries no authority — and adverseness travels in `local-review/summary`
(`failure` for unresolved findings), which is the gate's review evidence.

**Adjudication** (review.md §12) is a PR comment whose body starts with
`ADJUDICATION` and contains `head=<SHA>` for the current head, one disposition
line per remaining finding; `--adjudicated` takes nothing else.

**Idempotency.** Every publishing step is **at most one mutation**: a paginated
read finds the stable marker first and adopts that record instead of duplicating
it (`commentOnce`, issue-automation.yml:403-417, now guarding retries rather than
webhook redelivery); an ambiguous write stays pending for adoption.

## 3. The merge gate

`pr_merge.py <number>` is the only path to `main`: never `git merge` to main,
never push `main`. The merge is a REST `PUT …/pulls/{n}/merge` with the exact
`sha` guard, issued by `gh_common.merge_pr` and verified against the merge
commit's topology (two parents, the frozen head second), behind seven gates
that refuse by default:

1. the PR is open, unmerged and not a draft (`draft is False`, not merely
   falsy), and reports a head SHA, a head ref and a base ref;
2. the primary worktree is clean and on the base, and the local branch tip
   equals the GitHub head SHA — the merge must be of the bytes built here;
3. all eight `local-ci/<step>` contexts plus `local-ci/summary` are `success` on
   that exact SHA; a **missing** context blocks, because GitHub's combined state
   reads `success` for a commit carrying no statuses at all;
4. that SHA's marker-bound `COMMENT` review (or one carried forward per
   review.md §13) carries `VERDICT: APPROVED`, or
   `COMMENTED` with zero unchecked findings, **and** `local-review/summary` is
   `success` there;
5. no `CHANGES_REQUESTED` review stands on that head, from anyone;
6. no live fix lock for the branch (`locks/fix-<branch>.lock`, running holder);
   the count of `merge-base..head` commits whose subject starts with a §1 fix
   prefix is printed for the record and is not a gate;
7. every issue the PR body closes — all nine of GitHub's closing keywords, not
   just `Closes` — has no open sub-issue left.

`--adjudicated` waives gate 4's adverse verdict and nothing else, and only when
an exact-head `ADJUDICATION` comment backs it; gate 5 is never adjudicable.

Afterwards a best-effort, non-fatal tail fast-forwards local `main` to the
remote merge commit; branch and worktree cleanup keeps its safeguards (local
dirt defers it with a warning).

+/-- A uniform consistency defect is invariant under a bijective relabeling of
+its question type. -/
+theorem consistencyDefect_uniform_question_equiv
+    {X Y Outcome iota : Type*}
+    [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X] [Nonempty X]
+    [Fintype Y] [DecidableEq Y] [Nonempty Y]
+    [Fintype Outcome] [DecidableEq Outcome]
+    [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota]
+    (e : X ≃ Y) (A B : Y → Outcome → Op iota)
+    (psi : EuclideanSpace ℂ iota) :
+    consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution X)
+        (fun x a => A (e x) a) (fun x a => B (e x) a) psi =
+      consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution Y) A B psi := by
+  unfold consistencyDefect
+  simpa using avgOver_uniform_equiv e (fun x =>
+    ∑ a : Outcome, ∑ b : Outcome,
+      if a = b then 0 else
+        (inner ℂ psi ((EuclideanSpace.equiv iota ℂ).symm
+          (((A (e x) a) * (B (e x) b)).mulVec psi))).re)
+
+/-- A consistency defect is invariant under a bijective relabeling of both
+outcome families. -/
+theorem consistencyDefect_outcome_equiv
+    {X Alpha Beta iota : Type*}
+    [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X]
+    [Fintype Alpha] [DecidableEq Alpha]
+    [Fintype Beta] [DecidableEq Beta]
+    [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota]
+    (mu : Distribution X) (e : Beta ≃ Alpha)
+    (A B : X → Alpha → Op iota) (psi : EuclideanSpace ℂ iota) :
+    consistencyDefect mu
+        (fun x b => A x (e b)) (fun x b => B x (e b)) psi =
+      consistencyDefect mu A B psi := by
+  unfold consistencyDefect
+  apply avgOver_congr
+  intro x
+  let term : Alpha → Alpha → ℝ := fun a b =>
+    if a = b then 0 else
+      (inner ℂ psi ((EuclideanSpace.equiv iota ℂ).symm
+        (((A x a) * (B x b)).mulVec psi))).re
+  calc
+    _ = ∑ a : Beta, ∑ b : Beta, term (e a) (e b) := by
+      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
+      intro a _
+      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
+      intro b _
+      unfold term
+      by_cases hab : a = b
+      · subst b
+        simp
+      · have heab : e a ≠ e b := fun h => hab (e.injective h)
+        simp [hab, heab]
+    _ =
+        ∑ a : Beta, ∑ b : Alpha, term (e a) b := by
+      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl

# Formalization Patterns

Key design patterns used in the MIPStarRE Lean formalization to bridge the
gap between paper-level mathematics and a compilable Lean proof.

This document is intended for contributors who need to understand *why* the
Lean code is structured as it is, and for reviewers who need to recognize
these patterns when reading PRs.  It complements the individual chapter audits
in `audits/`, the proof-integrity rules in the lean-conventions skill (addenda:
`docs/project_conventions.md`), and the
proof-gap protocol in `docs/paper-gaps/proof-gap-protocol.tex`.

## Table of Contents

1. [Source-faithful statements and internal proof obligations](#pattern-1-source-faithful-statements-and-internal-proof-obligations)
2. [Blueprint–Lean synchronization](#pattern-2-blueprintlean-synchronization)
3. [Split-module architecture](#pattern-3-split-module-architecture)
4. [Public re-export pattern](#pattern-4-public-re-export-pattern)
5. [Temporary obligation-structure pattern](#pattern-5-temporary-obligation-structure-pattern)
6. [Paper-gap documentation pattern](#pattern-6-paper-gap-documentation-pattern)

## Pattern 1: Source-faithful statements and internal proof obligations

### The rule

A declaration presented as the formalization of a paper theorem, lemma,
proposition, or corollary must state the paper result, up to faithful formal
encoding of the mathematical domain.  Its public hypotheses and conclusion are
both part of the statement.  Adding a load-bearing bridge, residual, repair,
obligation-structure input, hypotheses bundle, or assumptions bundle not present
in the cited statement changes the theorem into a conditional helper.

The project therefore distinguishes three objects.

| Object | Public statement | Blueprint status |
|--------|------------------|------------------|
| Paper theorem | Matches the cited result in `references/ldt-paper/` | May be linked by source-labelled `\lean{}`; statement-level `\leanok` only when the statement matches |
| Internal proof obligation | Proves a missing intermediate mathematical input from paper hypotheses | May contain a tracked `sorry` while the proof is open |
| Conditional helper | Quarantines an unproved intermediate obligation | Not a paper theorem; no source-labelled `\leanok` |

It is never allowed to change the public statement of a declaration presented
as the formalization of a source-labelled paper theorem.  At the final assembly
point, the paper theorem must either discharge the extra hypotheses internally,
or remain as the paper-aligned statement with an unfinished proof while the
conditional helper is given a different name.

The preferred way to expose unfinished work is a named internal theorem or
definition with a precise paper-origin docstring and, if necessary, a tracked
`sorry`.  This makes the proof frontier visible without weakening the statement
of a source-labelled theorem.

### Why legacy scaffolding may remain temporarily

| Temporary reason | Explanation |
|------------------|-------------|
| **Localizing an obstruction** | A conditional helper can isolate the exact missing mathematical input while the obligation discharger is being proved. |
| **Recovering useful proof content** | The proof body may contain genuine estimates or constructions that should be extracted into source-faithful lemmas. |
| **Auditability** | An explicit temporary hypothesis is easier to find than an implicit assumption hidden in prose, provided it is named as proof debt. |

These reasons do not justify strengthening a paper theorem.  They only explain
why a short-lived helper declaration may exist while its remaining hypotheses
are being actively removed.

### How to proceed when a proof needs an extra input

1. **Check the source statement.**  Read the corresponding TeX in
   `references/ldt-paper/` before changing a theorem linked from the blueprint.
2. **Keep the paper-facing declaration source-faithful.**  Boundary hypotheses
   such as positivity, nonemptiness, decidability, field-model instances, or
   type-class assumptions may be faithful encodings when they are needed to
   state the mathematics in Lean.  Proof data such as `BridgeInputs`,
   `RepairInput`, `Residual`, `Package`, generic `Hypotheses`, or generic
   `Assumptions` is different: it is not a paper assumption unless the cited
   statement says so.
3. **Name the missing intermediate result.**  If the proof uses a mathematical
   fact not yet formalized, state it as a separate proof obligation.  A
   temporary `sorry` in this declaration is preferable to adding the obligation as
   a hypothesis on the paper theorem.
4. **Do not introduce conditional helpers by default.**  A helper whose name
   ends in `_ofObligations` is a quarantine device, not a normal formalization
   pattern.  It may remain temporarily only when it preserves substantial proof
   content that cannot yet be connected to the paper hypotheses, has a tracked
   discharge or deletion target, and has no source-labelled blueprint
   `\leanok`.  If the helper would merely package missing work as an extra
   hypothesis, restore the theorem with the paper statement and leave a tracked
   `sorry` instead.
5. **Audit the final statement.**  Every PR touching a source-labelled theorem
   should compare paper assumptions and Lean assumptions, paper conclusion and
   Lean conclusion, and report whether the Lean statement is exact, has only
   faithful boundary hypotheses, or has extra assumptions.

If a paper-facing declaration is temporarily proved by calling a conditional
helper whose load-bearing input has not yet been produced from the paper
hypotheses, the proof frontier must be marked explicitly.  The declaration
should carry an `**Unfaithful:**` docstring section naming the non-paper
dependency, citing the paper-gap note or tracking issue, and identifying the
internal theorem that will remove the dependency.  A named proof obligation
with a tracked `sorry` is preferred whenever possible, because it makes the
missing mathematical assertion visible without adding it to the paper theorem
statement.

### Required metadata for new proof-obligation declarations

A new declaration whose name contains a proof-debt token such as `Bridge`,
`Residual`, `Repair`, `Package`, `Producer`, `Input`, `Hypotheses`,
`Assumptions`, `Obligation`, or `Witness` must explain its mathematical role in
the def-site docstring.  A paper citation alone is not enough, because the
reviewer must be able to tell whether the declaration is part of the paper
statement or a Lean-only proof obligation.

Use one of the following markers.

| Marker | Use |
|--------|-----|
| `**Source:**`, `**Paper source:**`, or `**Source statement:**` | The declaration is a faithful formal encoding of a cited source statement or a field of that statement |
| `**Faithful encoding:**` | The declaration records boundary data or domain data that the paper uses implicitly |
| `**Proof obligation:**` or `**Internal proof obligation:**` | The declaration is a theorem or record that must be proved from the paper hypotheses before a source theorem is complete |
| `**Conditional:**` | The declaration is a conditional helper; it must not be linked as the source theorem |
| `**Unfaithful:**` | The declaration or proof currently depends on a load-bearing assumption not yet derived from the paper hypotheses |

Proof-obligation, conditional, and unfaithful markers must cite a paper-gap note
or tracking issue and must state the planned discharge or elimination theorem.
If such a declaration would merely package missing work as an added hypothesis
to a source theorem, do not introduce it; restore the source theorem statement
and leave the missing proof as a tracked `sorry`.

### Conditional helper boundary

1. **Prefer a source theorem with a tracked `sorry`.**  If a proof requires a
   construction that is not yet available from the paper hypotheses, the first
   repair is to restore the source theorem statement and leave the missing proof
   open.  Do not introduce a new `Input`, `Obligation`, `Residual`, `Repair`,
   `Producer`, or `Package` merely to avoid that `sorry`.

2. **Do not bundle several missing theorem-level steps into one hypothesis.**
   The former Section 9 bundle `SelfImprovementObligations` and the helper
   `selfImprovementFromObligations` were removed because they bundled
   helper strong self-consistency, orthonormalization, and final-field transport
   into a single route to the full self-improvement conclusion.  The correct
   boundary is now the theorem `selfImprovement`, whose missing
   proof is an explicit `sorry`.

   The former induction-section helper
   `selfImprovementInInductionSection_ofObligations` was removed because it
   encouraged propagation of the Section 9 bundle into the Section 6 successor
   constructors.  Those constructors now call the theorem
   `selfImprovementInInductionSection` directly; its current proof gap is the
   correct place for the missing work.

3. **Propagation is a warning sign.**  The consumer of
   `selfImprovementInInductionSection` — typically a
   `MainInductionStep` theorem — should close the hypothesis with an internal
   theorem as soon as possible.  If the hypothesis propagates upward toward a
   paper-labelled theorem, the PR should stop and either prove the obligation or
   restore the paper theorem with an explicit unfinished proof.

4. **Final closure at the paper theorem.**  The theorem `mainFormal` in
   `MIPStarRE/LDT/Test/MainTheorem/MainFormal.lean` is reserved for the
   paper-shaped statement.  If the witness needed by the final transport has
   not yet been constructed from the paper hypotheses, the theorem should remain
   an explicit unfinished proof.  Do not replace the missing construction by
   extra bridge, residual, repair, package, or obligation hypotheses, and do not
   proliferate named obligation declarations merely to avoid a direct `sorry`.

   The paper-labelled `mainFormal` should have the hypotheses of the paper
   theorem: a projective strategy passing the low individual degree test, the
   stated parameter bounds, and the faithful formalization of the ambient
   domains.  Bridge, residual, repair, and proof-obligation inputs must be
   produced inside its proof rather than added to its statement.

### Existing bridge-like declarations

Several older declarations still name proof obligations explicitly.  They are
transitional proof debt, not a pattern to extend to paper theorem statements.
When such a declaration remains useful, its role should be made explicit and
kept away from source-labelled blueprint entries.

| Declaration | Status to maintain |
|-------------|--------------------|
| `LdPastingNontrivialContext` | Nontrivial-regime context for `ldPastingNontrivial`; do not present it as the unrestricted `thm:ld-pasting` context |
| `Pasting.ldPastingNontrivial` | Restricted nontrivial-regime form of `thm:ld-pasting`; link from a Lean-only remark, while `Pasting.ldPasting` remains the unrestricted source-facing theorem |

The former same-carrier `mainFormal` transport-witness route has been retired.
The former `SelfImprovement.HelperStrongSelfConsistencyInput`,
`SelfImprovement.OrthonormalizationInput`, `SelfImprovement.FinalFieldsInput`, and
`MakingMeasurementsProjective.OrthonormalizationInput` bundles have been removed.
Useful proof content should be kept as named construction lemmas, while missing
orthonormalization or final-field arguments remain direct proof gaps on the
source-facing theorem until proved from the paper hypotheses.

The former `MakingMeasurementsProjective.SpectralTruncationInput` abbreviation

source-shaped statement `SpectralTruncationStatement` and by direct construction
theorems such as `spectralTruncationStatement_of_sourceAlmostProjective`,
rather than by an `Input` wrapper passed through later theorems.

An auxiliary declaration should be removed from the main blueprint route, or
renamed and documented as a purely internal lemma, when all of the following
conditions hold.

1. It is not a statement in the cited paper and is not an explicitly cited
   outside result.
2. No current proof of a paper-level target needs it as stated.
3. It assumes stronger proof data, finite-length data, completion data, repair

    20	`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:195-208`, paper `06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:232-248`. -/
    21	noncomputable def consistencyDefect {X α ι : Type*}
    22	    [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X] [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
    23	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    24	    (μ : Distribution X) (A B : X → α → Op ι)
    25	    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) : ℝ :=
    26	  avgOver μ (fun x =>
    27	    ∑ a : α, ∑ b : α,
    28	      if a = b then 0 else
    29	        (inner ℂ ψ ((EuclideanSpace.equiv ι ℂ).symm
    30	          ((A x a * B x b).mulVec ψ))).re)

    32	/-- A uniform consistency defect is invariant under a bijective relabeling of
    33	its question type. -/
    34	theorem consistencyDefect_uniform_question_equiv
    35	    {X Y Outcome iota : Type*}
    36	    [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X] [Nonempty X]
    37	    [Fintype Y] [DecidableEq Y] [Nonempty Y]
    38	    [Fintype Outcome] [DecidableEq Outcome]
    39	    [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota]
    40	    (e : X ≃ Y) (A B : Y → Outcome → Op iota)
    41	    (psi : EuclideanSpace ℂ iota) :
    42	    consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution X)
    43	        (fun x a => A (e x) a) (fun x a => B (e x) a) psi =
    44	      consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution Y) A B psi := by
    45	  unfold consistencyDefect
    46	  simpa using avgOver_uniform_equiv e (fun x =>
    47	    ∑ a : Outcome, ∑ b : Outcome,
    48	      if a = b then 0 else
    49	        (inner ℂ psi ((EuclideanSpace.equiv iota ℂ).symm
    50	          (((A (e x) a) * (B (e x) b)).mulVec psi))).re)
    51	
    52	/-- A consistency defect is invariant under a bijective relabeling of both
    53	outcome families. -/
    54	theorem consistencyDefect_outcome_equiv
    55	    {X Alpha Beta iota : Type*}
    56	    [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X]
    57	    [Fintype Alpha] [DecidableEq Alpha]
    58	    [Fintype Beta] [DecidableEq Beta]
    59	    [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota]
    60	    (mu : Distribution X) (e : Beta ≃ Alpha)
    61	    (A B : X → Alpha → Op iota) (psi : EuclideanSpace ℂ iota) :
    62	    consistencyDefect mu
    63	        (fun x b => A x (e b)) (fun x b => B x (e b)) psi =
    64	      consistencyDefect mu A B psi := by
    65	  unfold consistencyDefect
    66	  apply avgOver_congr
    67	  intro x
    68	  let term : Alpha → Alpha → ℝ := fun a b =>
    69	    if a = b then 0 else
    70	      (inner ℂ psi ((EuclideanSpace.equiv iota ℂ).symm
    71	        (((A x a) * (B x b)).mulVec psi))).re
    72	  calc
    73	    _ = ∑ a : Beta, ∑ b : Beta, term (e a) (e b) := by
    74	      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
    75	      intro a _
    76	      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
    77	      intro b _
    78	      unfold term
    79	      by_cases hab : a = b
    80	      · subst b
    81	        simp
    82	      · have heab : e a ≠ e b := fun h => hab (e.injective h)
    83	        simp [hab, heab]
    84	    _ =
    85	        ∑ a : Beta, ∑ b : Alpha, term (e a) b := by
    86	      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
    87	      intro a _
    88	      exact Equiv.sum_comp e (fun b => term (e a) b)
    89	    _ = ∑ a : Alpha, ∑ b : Alpha, term a b :=
    90	      Equiv.sum_comp e (fun a => ∑ b : Alpha, term a b)
    91	    _ = _ := rfl

   200	\section{Distance measures}
   201	
   202	\begin{definition}[Distance between states]\label{def:state-distance}
   203		Let $\{\ket{\psi_n}\}_{n \in \N}$ and $\{\ket{\psi'_n}\}_{n \in \N}$ be two families of states in the same space $\mathcal H$. For a function $\delta \colon \N \to [0,1]$ we say that $\{\ket{\psi_n}\}$ and $\{\ket{\psi'_n}\}$ are \emph{$\delta$-close}, denoted $\ket{\psi} \approx_\delta \ket{\psi'}$, if
   204		\[
   205			\lVert \ket{\psi_n} - \ket{\psi'_n} \rVert^2 = O(\delta(n))\,.
   206		\]
   207		The dependence of the states and of $\delta$ on the indexing parameter $n$ is generally left implicit; we write, e.g., $\ket{\psi}$ for $\ket{\psi_n}$.
   208	\end{definition}
   209	
   210	\begin{definition}[Consistency between POVMs]\label{def:consistency}
   211		\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.consistencyDefect, MIPStarRE.QPBT.IsConsistentWithin}
   212		\leanok
   213		\uses{def:povm-conventions, def:state-distance}
   214		Let $\mathcal X$ be a finite set and $\mu$ a distribution on $\mathcal X$. Let $\ket{\psi} \in \mathcal H_A \ot \mathcal H_B$ be a quantum state, and for all $x \in \mathcal X$ let $\{A^x_a\}$ and $\{B^x_a\}$ be POVMs. We write
   215		\[
   216			A^x_a \ot \Id_B \simeq_\delta \Id_A \ot B^x_a
   217		\]
   218		on state $\ket{\psi}$ and distribution $\mu$ if
   219		\[
   220			\E_{x \sim \mu} \sum_{a \ne b} \bra{\psi} A^x_a \ot B^x_b \ket{\psi} = O(\delta)\,.
   221		\]
   222		In this case we say that $\{A^x_a\}$ and $\{B^x_a\}$ are \emph{$\delta$-consistent} on $\ket{\psi}$. As in Definition~\ref{def:state-distance}, the $O(\cdot)$ refers to families of POVMs and states indexed by an implicit parameter $n \in \N$, and is taken as $n \to \infty$.
   223	\end{definition}
   224	
   225	A measurement that is consistent on $\ket{\psi}$ in the sense of Definition~\ref{def:consistent-measurement} is $0$-consistent with itself on the same state under the singleton distribution, and vice versa: if $\sum_a \bra{\psi} M_a \ot M_a \ket{\psi} = 1$, then $M_a \ot \Id\, \ket{\psi} = \Id \ot M_a\, \ket{\psi}$ for every $a$, by the equality case of the Cauchy--Schwarz inequality applied outcome by outcome.
   250			\item For all $x \in \mathcal X$ and $y \in \mathcal Y$, we have $A^x_a \approx_\delta (A')^x_a$ and $B^y_b \approx_\delta (B')^y_b$, with the approximations holding under the distribution $\mu$ (i.e.\ under its corresponding marginals), on either $\ket{\psi}$ or $\ket{\psi'}$.
   251		\end{enumerate}
   252	\end{definition}
   253	
   254	\begin{remark}[Asymptotic reading of the distance relations]\label{rem:asymptotic-distance}
   255		Definitions~\ref{def:state-distance}, \ref{def:consistency}, and \ref{def:povm-distance} are asymptotic: every $\approx_\delta$ and $\simeq_\delta$ statement refers to families of states and measurement families indexed by an implicit parameter $n \in \N$, and the $O(\cdot)$ is taken as $n \to \infty$. None of these relations is a pointwise inequality with an explicit constant. By contrast, the corresponding relations used in the low individual degree chapters (Definitions~\ref{def:simeq} and~\ref{def:approx_delta}) carry no hidden constant. Any explicit quantitative version of the present relations therefore retains the constants absorbed into the $O(\cdot)$; for instance, the triangle inequality of Lemma~\ref{fact:triangle} carries a factor $2$ inside the $O(\cdot)$.
   256	\end{remark}

    29	/-- Relabel a matrix measurement along an equivalence of outcome alphabets. -/
    30	noncomputable def matrixMeasurementTransport
    31	    {alpha beta iota : Type*}
    32	    [Fintype alpha] [Fintype beta] [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota]
    33	    (e : alpha ≃ beta) (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement alpha iota) :
    34	    MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement beta iota :=
    35	  MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement.ofSumEqOne
    36	    (fun b => M.effect (e.symm b))
    37	    (fun b => M.pos (e.symm b))
    38	    (by
    39	      calc
    40	        ∑ b, M.effect (e.symm b) = ∑ a, M.effect a :=
    41	          Equiv.sum_comp e.symm M.effect
    42	        _ = 1 := M.sum_eq_one)
    43

    45	    {alpha beta iota : Type*}
    46	    [Fintype alpha] [Fintype beta] [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota]
    47	    (e : alpha ≃ beta) (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement alpha iota)
    48	    (b : beta) :
    49	    (matrixMeasurementTransport e M).effect b = M.effect (e.symm b) :=
    50	  rfl

    54	    {alpha beta iota : Type*}
    55	    [Fintype alpha] [Fintype beta] [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota]
    56	    (e : alpha ≃ beta) (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement alpha iota)
    57	    (hM : MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective M) :

    61	/-- Assemble a family of matrix measurements as diagonal blocks indexed by a
    62	finite classical register. -/
    63	noncomputable def blockDiagonalMeasurement
    64	    {alpha iota block : Type*}
    65	    [Fintype alpha] [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota]
    66	    [Fintype block] [DecidableEq block]
    67	    (M : block → MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement alpha iota) :
    68	    MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement alpha (iota × block) :=
    69	  MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement.ofSumEqOne
    70	    (fun a => Matrix.blockDiagonal fun r => (M r).effect a)
    71	    (fun a => Matrix.blockDiagonal_nonneg
    72	      (fun r => (M r).effect a) (fun r => (M r).pos a))
    73	    (by
    74	      ext ⟨i, r⟩ ⟨j, s⟩
    75	      simp only [Matrix.sum_apply, Matrix.blockDiagonal_apply]
    76	      by_cases hrs : r = s
    77	      · subst s
    78	        simp only [if_pos]
    79	        calc
    80	          ∑ x, (M r).effect x i j = (1 : Matrix iota iota ℂ) i j :=
    81	            by
    82	              simpa only [Matrix.sum_apply] using
    83	                congrFun (congrFun (M r).sum_eq_one i) j
    84	          _ = (1 : Matrix (iota × block) (iota × block) ℂ)
    85	              (i, r) (j, r) := by
    86	                change (if i = j then 1 else 0) =
    87	                  (if (i, r) = (j, r) then 1 else 0)
    88	                simp
    89	      · simp [hrs])

    95	    (M : block → MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement alpha iota)
    96	    (a : alpha) :

   101	/-- A block-diagonal family of projective measurements is projective. -/
   102	theorem blockDiagonalMeasurement_isProjective
   103	    {alpha iota block : Type*}
   104	    [Fintype alpha] [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota]
   105	    [Fintype block] [DecidableEq block]
   106	    (M : block → MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement alpha iota)
   107	    (hM : ∀ r, MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective (M r)) :
   108	    MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective (blockDiagonalMeasurement M) := by
   109	  intro a
   110	  constructor
   111	  · change Matrix.blockDiagonal (fun r => (M r).effect a) *
   112	        Matrix.blockDiagonal (fun r => (M r).effect a) =
   113	      Matrix.blockDiagonal (fun r => (M r).effect a)
   114	    rw [← Matrix.blockDiagonal_mul]
   115	    congr 1
   116	    funext r
   117	    exact (hM r a).isIdempotentElem.eq
   118	  · change (Matrix.blockDiagonal (fun r => (M r).effect a))ᴴ =
   119	      Matrix.blockDiagonal (fun r => (M r).effect a)
   120	    rw [Matrix.blockDiagonal_conjTranspose]
   121	    congr 1
   122	    funext r
   123	    exact (hM r a).isSelfAdjoint.star_eq

   143	/-- Reindexing Euclidean coordinates along an equivalence preserves norm. -/
   144	theorem reindexState_norm_eq
   145	    {iota kappa : Type*}
   146	    [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota]
   147	    [Fintype kappa] [DecidableEq kappa]
   148	    (e : iota ≃ kappa) (psi : EuclideanSpace ℂ iota) :
   149	    ‖reindexState e psi‖ = ‖psi‖ := by
   150	  rw [← sq_eq_sq₀ (norm_nonneg _) (norm_nonneg _)]
   151	  rw [EuclideanSpace.norm_sq_eq, EuclideanSpace.norm_sq_eq]
   152	  change (∑ j : kappa, ‖psi (e.symm j)‖ ^ 2) = ∑ i : iota, ‖psi i‖ ^ 2
   153	  exact e.symm.sum_comp (fun i => ‖psi i‖ ^ 2)

   155	/-- The coordinate tensor of two Euclidean vectors has the product norm. -/
   156	theorem vecTensor_norm_eq
   157	    {iota kappa : Type*}
   158	    [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota]
   159	    [Fintype kappa] [DecidableEq kappa]
   160	    (u : EuclideanSpace ℂ iota) (v : EuclideanSpace ℂ kappa) :
   161	    ‖vecTensor u v‖ = ‖u‖ * ‖v‖ := by
   162	  rw [← sq_eq_sq₀ (norm_nonneg _) (mul_nonneg (norm_nonneg _) (norm_nonneg _))]
   163	  rw [EuclideanSpace.norm_sq_eq, mul_pow, EuclideanSpace.norm_sq_eq,

   165	  change (∑ p : iota × kappa, ‖u p.1 * v p.2‖ ^ 2) =

   168	  rw [← Finset.univ_product_univ, Finset.sum_product, Finset.sum_mul]

    66	\section{Combined point measurements}
    67	
    68	The measurements $\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point},X),x}$ and
    69	$\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point},Z),z}$ commute only approximately. The first goal of
    70	this chapter is to construct a single projective measurement that
    71	simultaneously measures both, first at points and then along lines. The
    72	construction of the combined point measurement proceeds in three steps: the
    73	binary refinements $\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point},X),x,r}$ and
    74	$\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point},Z),z,s}$ are combined into a sandwich POVM, the
    75	resulting family is shown to satisfy an approximate linearity in the index

    77	Vidick~\cite{Natarajan2017Linearity} converts approximate linearity into exact
    78	linearity, from which a projective measurement with outcomes in $\F_q^2$ is
    79	assembled by Fourier averaging.

    57

  2046		statement of Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-4-7} is phrased, with $a > 1$ and
  2047		$0 < b < 1$. The discrepancy is harmless: enlarging $a$ and shrinking
  2048		$b$ only weakens a bound of this form, so any admissible pair for
  2049		Theorem~\ref{lem:ld-soundness} yields an admissible pair for
  2050		Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-4-7}. The closing computation of the source proof
  2051		also mixes the terms $d/q$ and $md/q$ in the bound for $\delta_S$; the
  2052		weaker $md/q$ is the one recorded above.
  2053	\end{remark}

    38	      consistencyDefect
    39	          (uniformDistribution (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D))
    40	          (fun u a => heteroKron
    41	            ((directPointCoordinateMeasurementA D S r u).effect a) 1)
    42	          (fun u a => heteroKron 1
    43	            ((directPolynomialEvaluationMeasurement D G u).effect a)) S.ψ =
    44	        consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution (Point D.toLDTParameters))
    45	          (ldtPointAPlaced D S hS r)
    46	          (ldtPolynomialEvaluationRight D G) S.ψ := by
    47	  letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
    48	  intro G

    50	    consistencyDefect
    51	        (uniformDistribution (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D))

# Mathematical Language Guidelines

MIPStarRE Lean names and documentation should be written for readers comparing
the formalization with the paper and blueprint.

This is a project-local supplement to the Mathlib-derived documentation,
naming, and style guides in the lean-conventions skill's `MATHLIB_doc`,
`MATHLIB_naming`, and `MATHLIB_style` references.

## Scope

These guidelines apply to:

- public Lean declaration names and namespace names;
- module docstrings;
- declaration docstrings;
- documentation-visible section comments;
- explanatory comments that describe the mathematical role of a declaration.
- blueprint prose and formalization-support notes;
- issue titles and issue bodies;
- PR titles and PR descriptions.

## Source of Truth

Use terminology from the following sources, in this order:

1. `references/ldt-paper/`
2. `blueprint/src/chapter/`
3. established local conventions in nearby Lean files

When the paper has a term for the object, use that term. For Section 5, for
example, prefer orthogonalization lemma, truncation function, rounding to
projectors, rank reduction, and completing to measurement.

## Reference Notation And Terminology

The notation and terminology of the original reference are the default for
reader-facing mathematical text.  A reader should be able to compare a Lean
docstring, blueprint paragraph, issue, or PR description with the cited source
without first learning a private vocabulary used by the formalization.

When Lean must use a different name or representation, define the deviation in a
location which future readers can find from the affected statement.  Use the
first applicable location in the following order:

1. the declaration docstring of the public object whose name or representation
   differs from the paper;
2. the module docstring of the defining Lean file, when the deviation concerns a
   family of declarations in that file;
3. the relevant blueprint paragraph, when the notation appears only in the
   blueprint;
4. a report under `docs/reports/` or `docs/paper-gaps/`, when the deviation is a
   larger discrepancy between the paper, blueprint, and Lean.

The explanation should say:

- the notation or term used in the paper;
- the Lean object or name which represents it;
- the mathematical reason for the difference, if there is one;
- the scope in which the replacement should be used.

A PR description may mention the deviation, but it should not be the only place
where future readers can learn it.

Formalization-only auxiliary lemmas should be introduced as such.  Their prose
should name the nearby paper equation, theorem, or construction they support,
rather than presenting the auxiliary name as paper terminology.

## Naming Norm

Names and prose should describe the mathematical object, hypothesis, or
conclusion. They should not encode the history of how the formalization was
assembled.

Avoid presenting words such as `pipeline`, `wrapper`, `package`, `raw`,
`oneShot`, or `liveBlock` as mathematical terminology unless the cited source
uses them with that meaning. Likewise, avoid implementation-local substitutes
such as `projectivization` or `spectral truncation` when the paper gives a
clearer phrase.

This is a general rule for the repository, not only a rule for file splits.
Module names, namespace names, public declarations, theorem fields, docstrings,
blueprint-facing names, issue titles, and spec documents should name the
mathematical layer under discussion, not the local workflow step, paper line
number, or implementation history.

### Concrete examples

The table below illustrates the naming norm with examples patterned on the
codebase and on names seen during review.  Some entries are existing names;
others are proposed names for future refactors.  The "avoid" column lists
process-shaped names that encode the history of how the formalization was
assembled; the "prefer" column lists mathematical names that a reader of the
paper or blueprint would recognize.

| Avoid (process-shaped)                        | Prefer (mathematical)                     | Rationale                                              |
|:----------------------------------------------|:------------------------------------------|:-------------------------------------------------------|
| `Line130`                                     | `ProjectiveConsistency`                   | Paper Lemma 5.13, not "the line-130 identity"          |
| `Line169`                                     | `CompletionTransport`                     | Paper Lemma 5.16, step that transports completed data  |
| `Step6`                                       | `Orthonormalization`                      | Paper Section 5, the orthonormalization construction   |
| `FinalAssembly`                               | `DiagonalCompletion`                      | Paper Lemma 5.17, constructing a diagonal POVM         |
| `OneShotIneq`                                 | `SelfConsistencyDataProcessing` (or existing module `Preliminaries.SelfConsistency.DataProcessing`)           | Paper's data-processing inequality for self-consistency |
| `PipelineCheck`                               | `ErrorPropagationBound` (proposed)                   | The bound that propagates error through the test       |
| `QxpLayerWrapper`                             | `ProjectivePOVMCompletion` (proposed)                | The construction from round-projectors to POVMs        |
| `RawSpectralTruncation`                       | `SpectralTruncation`                      | The paper's spectral truncation, not an "unwrapped" version |
| `AddInUStep3To5`                              | `AddInUUpperExcessMass` (proposed)                  | Paper Addendum in §U, the upper excess-mass estimate   |
| `AddInUStep12`                                | `AddInUCommutationTail` (proposed)                   | Paper Addendum in §U, the commutation tail estimate    |

An avoided name is acceptable only when the cited paper itself uses that
phrase as the mathematical name (e.g., a lemma the paper calls "Step 2").
In that case the docstring should cite the paper's phrasing.

File-split PRs are a common place where this rule matters: new leaves should be
named by the mathematical boundary they isolate, and any public declarations
exposed by the split should be reviewed under the same standard.

### Shared helpers

When the same (or nearly the same) helper declaration appears in two or
more chapter-local leaves, the copies should be consolidated into a single
shared helper in an appropriate common module.  This avoids duplication and
ensures that fixes, generalizations, or upstream replacements apply to all
call sites at once.  Issue [#1145] tracks this work across the repository.

Procedure:

1. **Confirm equivalence.**  Compare the statement of each copy.  If the
   types differ only by a chapter-specific parameterization (e.g.,
   `SubMeas (Polynomial params) ι` vs `SubMeas (Point params) ι`),
   parameterize the shared helper over that type via a `variable` or
   explicit argument.
2. **Find the right home.**  Prefer a module that is already imported by
   both call sites.  Typical candidates:
   - `MIPStarRE/LDT/Basic/` for parameter-free operators and bounds,
   - `MIPStarRE/LDT/Preliminaries/` for polynomial/field/character lemmas,
   - The highest chapter that is a common dependency of the two sites.
3. **Name mathematically.**  Give the shared helper a name that describes
   what it states, not which chapter it originally came from.
4. **Replace call sites.**  Delete the chapter-local copies and replace
   their uses with the shared helper.  A thin wrapper is allowed only when it
   preserves a paper-facing or blueprint-facing name that external readers
   need to search for; such wrappers should have a docstring or compatibility
   comment explaining why the alias exists.  Remove the wrapper once that
   paper-facing name is no longer needed for external reference.
5. **Document.**  Add a docstring to the shared helper citing the paper or
   blueprint location it supports.

### Legacy identifier treatment

If a docstring must mention a legacy Lean identifier, cite it in backticks and
describe the mathematical object in paper terminology. If an old public
identifier cannot be renamed in the current PR, record the required migration
in the issue, PR description, or an audit file under `audits/`.

Do not add an empty pass-through abbreviation merely to introduce a second
public name.  This is different from a documented public wrapper allowed in the
shared-helper procedure above: a wrapper must preserve a paper-facing or
blueprint-facing term and must say why the alias exists.

## Review Checklist

Reviewers should use this checklist when examining public names and
documentation prose.  Flag any item that fails.

- [ ] **Naming.**  Do public declaration names, namespace names, module names,
      theorem field names, and docstring prose describe a mathematical object,
      hypothesis, or conclusion?  Or do they encode the history of how the
      formalization was assembled (paper line numbers, workflow steps,
      implementation-phase labels)?
- [ ] **Source alignment.**  For the mathematical content under review, does
      the prose use the terminology in `references/ldt-paper/` or the
      blueprint?  Are process words such as `pipeline`, `wrapper`, `package`,
      `raw`, `oneShot`, or `liveBlock` used as mathematical terms when the
      source does not use them that way?
- [ ] **Deviation documented.**  If a Lean name or representation differs from
      the paper, is the deviation documented in a declaration docstring,
      module docstring, blueprint paragraph, or `docs/paper-gaps/` note, in
      that order of preference?
- [ ] **Auxiliary lemmas.**  Are formalization-only auxiliary lemmas introduced
      as such, with prose naming the nearby paper equation, theorem, or
      construction they support?
- [ ] **Shared helpers.**  Does the PR introduce a helper that already exists
      (or near-exists) in another chapter-local leaf?  If so, has it been
      consolidated into a common module with a mathematical name?
- [ ] **Legacy IDs.**  If a legacy Lean identifier is mentioned, is the
      mathematical object described in paper terminology?  If an old public
      identifier cannot be renamed yet, is the required migration recorded in
      the issue, PR description, or an audit file?
- [ ] **Pass-through names.**  Does the PR add an empty pass-through
      abbreviation that introduces a second public name without adding
      mathematical content?  Reject it unless it is a documented compatibility
      wrapper preserving paper-facing or blueprint-facing terminology.

Review-fix PRs touching a surface covered by an active audit should read the
relevant audit before changing names or prose.

[#1145]: https://github.com/LionSR/MIPStarRE/issues/1145

     5	/-!
     6	# Geometry for the directly indexed low-degree game
     7	
     8	This module defines the parameters, line carrier, and line-point distributions
     9	for the directly indexed low-degree game.
    10	
    11	## References
    12	
    13	The line-point distributions originate in
    14	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:243-272`.
    15	The directly indexed repair is documented in
    16	`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility.tex`.
    17	-/

    19	open scoped BigOperators
    20

    27	noncomputable section
    28	
    29	/-- Parameters for the directly indexed low-degree game.  Unlike `LdParams`,
    30	this directly indexed line-space construction has no divisibility field: its coordinate index is
    31	sampled from `Fin m` rather than encoded by fibers of `chiIndex`.
    32	
    33	This is the direct-index repair described in
    34	`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility.tex`; it is not a second
    35	definition of the source verifier game. -/
    36	structure DirectLdParams where
    37	  q : ℕ
    38	  m : ℕ
    39	  d : ℕ
    40	  k : ℕ
    41	  hm : 1 ≤ m
    42	  hd : 1 ≤ d
    43	  hk : 1 ≤ k
    44	  hq : IsAdmissibleSize q
    45	
    46	/-- The canonical scalar model for directly indexed parameters. -/
    47	noncomputable def DirectLdParams.model (D : DirectLdParams) : FixedFieldModel D.q :=
    48	  fixedFieldModel D.q D.hq
    49	
    50	/-- The scalar field of a directly indexed low-degree game. -/
    51	abbrev DirectScalarQ (D : DirectLdParams) := D.model.K
    52	
    53	/-- The first coordinate, available because directly indexed dimensions are
    54	positive. -/
    55	def DirectLdParams.firstIndex (D : DirectLdParams) : Fin D.m :=
    56	  ⟨0, lt_of_lt_of_le Nat.zero_lt_one D.hm⟩
    57	
    58	instance (D : DirectLdParams) : Nonempty (Fin D.m) := ⟨D.firstIndex⟩
    59	
    60	/-- The direct game used at the extended dimension of the combining map.  Its
    61	field, degree, and simultaneity parameters are inherited from `P`, while its
    62	dimension is `2 * P.m + 2`; no divisibility assertion is introduced.
    63	
    64	The construction has dimension `2 * P.m + 2` without requiring
    65	`2 * P.m + 2 ∣ P.q`; it supplies the directly indexed line and coordinate
    66	spaces used in the dimension-extension argument of
    67	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:1257-1293`.
    68	-/
    69	def AdmissibleParams.extendedDirectLd (P : AdmissibleParams) : DirectLdParams where
    70	  q := P.q
    71	  m := 2 * P.m + 2
    72	  d := P.d
    73	  k := 1
    74	  hm := by omega
    75	  hd := P.hd
    76	  hk := by decide
    77	  hq := P.hq
    78	
    79	/-- A common random sample for the directly indexed question distribution.
    80	The point, coordinate index, and unrestricted direction are mutually uniform. -/

    82	  point : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D

    93	    DirectLdSpace D ≃

    95	        (Fin D.m × (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D)) where
    96	  toFun sample := (sample.point, sample.index, sample.direction)
    97	  invFun sample := ⟨sample.1, sample.2.1, sample.2.2⟩

   119	/-- Zero the coordinates preceding the directly sampled prefix index. -/
   120	def directPrefixProjection {D : DirectLdParams} (i : Fin D.m)
   121	    (v : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D :=
   122	  fun j => if j.val < i.val then 0 else v j

   124	/-- Canonical line descriptions whose coordinate index is stored directly.
   125	Coordinates are numbered from zero, so `index = i` represents coordinate
   126	`i + 1` in the paper. -/
   127	inductive DirectLineDesc (D : DirectLdParams) where
   128	  | axis (base : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) (index : Fin D.m)
   129	      (baseFixed : lineRepMap (coordinateDirection index) base = base)
   130	  | diagonal (base : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) (index : Fin D.m)
   131	      (direction : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D)
   132	      (baseFixed : lineRepMap direction base = base)
   133	      (prefixZero : ∀ j : Fin D.m, j.val < index.val → direction j = 0)
   134	  deriving DecidableEq

   136	/-- The kind of a directly indexed line. -/
   137	def DirectLineDesc.kind {D : DirectLdParams} : DirectLineDesc D → LineKind
   138	  | .axis _ _ _ => .axis
   139	  | .diagonal _ _ _ _ _ => .diagonal
   140	
   141	/-- The coordinate index stored in a directly indexed line. -/
   142	def DirectLineDesc.index {D : DirectLdParams} : DirectLineDesc D → Fin D.m
   143	  | .axis _ index _ => index
   144	  | .diagonal _ index _ _ _ => index
   145	
   146	/-- The canonical base point of a directly indexed line. -/
   147	def DirectLineDesc.base {D : DirectLdParams} :
   148	    DirectLineDesc D → Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D
   149	  | .axis base _ _ => base
   150	  | .diagonal base _ _ _ _ => base
   151	
   152	/-- The geometric direction of a directly indexed line. -/
   153	def DirectLineDesc.direction {D : DirectLdParams} (line : DirectLineDesc D) :
   154	    Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D :=
   155	  match line with
   156	  | .axis _ index _ => coordinateDirection index
   157	  | .diagonal _ _ direction _ _ => direction
   158	
   159	/-- The base of a directly indexed description is fixed by its geometric
   160	direction. -/
   161	theorem DirectLineDesc.base_fixed {D : DirectLdParams} (line : DirectLineDesc D) :
   162	    lineRepMap line.direction line.base = line.base := by
   163	  cases line with
   164	  | axis base index baseFixed => exact baseFixed
   165	  | diagonal base index direction baseFixed prefixZero => exact baseFixed
   166	
   167	/-- Every directly indexed diagonal description retains its prefix-zero
   168	invariant. -/
   169	theorem DirectLineDesc.diagonal_prefix_zero {D : DirectLdParams}
   170	    (line : DirectLineDesc D) (hline : line.kind = .diagonal) :
   171	    ∀ j : Fin D.m, j.val < line.index.val → line.direction j = 0 := by
   172	  cases line with
   173	  | axis base index baseFixed => simp [DirectLineDesc.kind] at hline
   174	  | diagonal base index direction baseFixed prefixZero => exact prefixZero
   175	
   176	/-- The point set represented by a directly indexed line. -/
   177	noncomputable def DirectLineDesc.pointSet {D : DirectLdParams}
   178	    (line : DirectLineDesc D) : Set (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) :=
   179	  linePoints line.base line.direction
   180	
   181	/-- Turn a direct sample into its canonical axis-line description. -/
   182	noncomputable def directALineDescOf (D : DirectLdParams)
   183	    (sample : DirectLdSpace D) : DirectLineDesc D :=
   184	  let direction := coordinateDirection sample.index
   185	  let base := lineRepMap direction sample.point
   186	  .axis base sample.index (lineRepMap_apply_self direction sample.point)
   187	
   188	/-- Turn a direct sample into its canonical diagonal-line description. -/
   189	noncomputable def directDLineDescOf (D : DirectLdParams)
   190	    (sample : DirectLdSpace D) : DirectLineDesc D :=
   191	  let direction := directPrefixProjection sample.index sample.direction
   192	  let base := lineRepMap direction sample.point
   193	  .diagonal base sample.index direction
   194	    (lineRepMap_apply_self direction sample.point) (by
   195	      intro j hj
   196	      change directPrefixProjection sample.index sample.direction j = 0
   197	      rw [directPrefixProjection, if_pos hj])
   198	
   199	/-- The axis-line/point law with a directly sampled coordinate index. -/
   200	noncomputable def directALinePointDist (D : DirectLdParams) :
   201	    Distribution (DirectLineDesc D × (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D)) :=
   202	  (uniformDistribution (DirectLdSpace D)).map fun sample =>
   203	    (directALineDescOf D sample, sample.point)
   204	
   205	/-- The diagonal-line/point law with a directly sampled prefix index. -/
   206	noncomputable def directDLinePointDist (D : DirectLdParams) :
   207	    Distribution (DirectLineDesc D × (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D)) :=
   208	  (uniformDistribution (DirectLdSpace D)).map fun sample =>
   209	    (directDLineDescOf D sample, sample.point)
   210	
   211	/-- The equal mixture of the directly indexed axis and diagonal line-point
   212	laws.  This is the replacement for the otherwise undefined extended-dimension
   213	instance used at paper
   214	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1020-1116`. -/
   215	noncomputable def directLinePointDist (D : DirectLdParams) :
   216	    Distribution (DirectLineDesc D × (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D)) :=
   217	  Distribution.mix (1 / 2) (by norm_num) (by norm_num)
   218	    (directALinePointDist D) (directDLinePointDist D)
   219	
   220	/-- The directly indexed axis-line/point law is probabilistic. -/
   221	theorem directALinePointDist_isProbability (D : DirectLdParams) :
   222	    (directALinePointDist D).IsProbability := by
   223	  exact (uniformDistribution_isProbability (DirectLdSpace D)).map _
   224	
   225	/-- The directly indexed diagonal-line/point law is probabilistic. -/
   226	theorem directDLinePointDist_isProbability (D : DirectLdParams) :
   227	    (directDLinePointDist D).IsProbability := by
   228	  exact (uniformDistribution_isProbability (DirectLdSpace D)).map _
   229	
   230	/-- The directly indexed line-point mixture is probabilistic. -/
   231	theorem directLinePointDist_isProbability (D : DirectLdParams) :
   232	    (directLinePointDist D).IsProbability := by
   233	  exact Distribution.mix_isProbability _ _ _
   234	    (directALinePointDist_isProbability D) (directDLinePointDist_isProbability D)
   235	    (by norm_num) (by norm_num)

     4	/-!
     5	# Strategy transport for the directly indexed low-degree game
     6	
     7	This module reads one coordinate of a projective directly indexed strategy as
     8	a two-space mature low individual degree strategy.  The question and answer
     9	transport of `Transport.Questions` supplies the canonical direct question of
    10	every mature line, with the reversed coordinate order and the leading index
    11	of the decoded diagonal direction, together with answer readouts that are
    12	covariant under line rebasing; this establishes all four covariance
    13	conditions of `ProjStrat`.  The module also records exact Born-weight
    14	formulas for both directions of strategy transport.
    15	
    16	## References
    17	
    18	- `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-458`
    19	- `references/ldt-paper/test_definition.tex:49-151`
    20	- `docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility.tex`
    21	-/

    34	/-- Regard a matrix-valued projective measurement as a projective measurement
    35	in the mature LDT interface. -/
    36	noncomputable def matrixMeasurementToLDTProjMeas
    37	    {alpha iota : Type*} [Fintype alpha] [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota]
    38	    (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement alpha iota)
    39	    (hM : MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective M) :
    40	    MIPStarRE.LDT.ProjMeas alpha iota where
    41	  toMeasurement := {
    42	    toSubMeas := {
    43	      outcome := M.effect
    44	      total := 1
    45	      outcome_pos := M.pos
    46	      sum_eq_total := M.sum_eq_one
    47	      total_le_one := le_rfl
    48	    }
    49	    total_eq_one := rfl
    50	  }
    51	  proj a := (hM a).isIdempotentElem.eq
    52	
    53	@[simp] theorem matrixMeasurementToLDTProjMeas_outcome
    54	    {alpha iota : Type*} [Fintype alpha] [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota]
    55	    (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement alpha iota)
    56	    (hM : MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective M) (a : alpha) :
    57	    (matrixMeasurementToLDTProjMeas M hM).outcome a = M.effect a :=
    58	  rfl

    60	/-- Point measurements obtained by querying the direct strategy and reading
    61	one simultaneous coordinate. -/
    62	noncomputable def directCoordinatePointMeasurement
    63	    (D : DirectLdParams) (r : Fin D.k)
    64	    {iota : Type*} [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota]
    65	    (M : DirectLdQuestion D →
    66	      MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement (DirectLdAnswer D) iota)
    67	    (hM : ∀ q, MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective (M q)) :
    68	    letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
    69	    IdxProjMeas (Point D.toLDTParameters) (Fq D.toLDTParameters) iota := by
    70	  letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
    71	  intro u
    72	  exact ProjMeas.postprocess
    73	    (matrixMeasurementToLDTProjMeas (M (directPointQuestionOf D u))
    74	      (hM (directPointQuestionOf D u)))
    75	    (directPointAnswerReadout D r)

   113	/-- The coordinate axis-line family is independent of the chosen affine
   114	parametrization of a mature line. -/
   115	theorem directCoordinateAxisMeasurement_reparam
   116	    (D : DirectLdParams) (r : Fin D.k)
   117	    {iota : Type*} [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota]
   118	    (M : DirectLdQuestion D →
   119	      MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement (DirectLdAnswer D) iota)
   120	    (hM : ∀ q, MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective (M q)) :
   121	    letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   122	    AxisParallelMeasurementReparamInvariant D.toLDTParameters
   123	      (directCoordinateAxisMeasurement D r M hM) := by
   124	  letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   125	  classical
   126	  intro line t f
   127	  simp only [directCoordinateAxisMeasurement, ProjMeas.postprocess,
   128	    SubMeas.postprocess_outcome, matrixMeasurementToLDTProjMeas_outcome]
   129	  rw [directAxisQuestionOf_rebase]
   130	  have hfiber :
   131	      Finset.univ.filter (fun answer =>
   132	        directAxisAnswerReadout D r (line.rebaseAt t) answer =
   133	          AxisLinePolynomial.reparamAt f t) =
   134	        Finset.univ.filter (fun answer =>
   135	          directAxisAnswerReadout D r line answer = f) := by
   136	    ext answer
   137	    simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and]
   138	    rw [directAxisAnswerReadout_rebase]
   139	    exact (AxisLinePolynomial.reparamAtEquiv t).injective.eq_iff
   140	  rw [hfiber]

   142	/-- The coordinate diagonal-line family is independent of the chosen affine
   143	parametrization, including the zero-direction convention. -/
   144	theorem directCoordinateDiagonalMeasurement_reparam
   145	    (D : DirectLdParams) (r : Fin D.k)
   146	    {iota : Type*} [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota]
   147	    (M : DirectLdQuestion D →
   148	      MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement (DirectLdAnswer D) iota)
   149	    (hM : ∀ q, MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective (M q)) :
   150	    letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   151	    DiagonalMeasurementReparamInvariant D.toLDTParameters
   152	      (directCoordinateDiagonalMeasurement D r M hM) := by
   153	  letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   154	  classical
   155	  intro line t f
   156	  simp only [directCoordinateDiagonalMeasurement, ProjMeas.postprocess,
   157	    SubMeas.postprocess_outcome, matrixMeasurementToLDTProjMeas_outcome]
   158	  rw [directDiagonalQuestionOf_rebase]
   159	  have hfiber :
   160	      Finset.univ.filter (fun answer =>
   161	        directDiagonalAnswerReadout D r (line.rebaseAt t) answer =
   162	          DiagonalLinePolynomial.reparamAt f t) =
   163	        Finset.univ.filter (fun answer =>
   164	          directDiagonalAnswerReadout D r line answer = f) := by
   165	    ext answer
   166	    simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and]
   167	    rw [directDiagonalAnswerReadout_rebase]
   168	    exact (DiagonalLinePolynomial.reparamAtEquiv t).injective.eq_iff
   169	  rw [hfiber]

   171	private theorem strategy_carrier_nonempty {G : Game} (S : Strategy G) :
   172	    Nonempty (S.ιA × S.ιB) := by
   173	  by_contra h
   174	  rw [not_nonempty_iff] at h
   175	  letI := h
   176	  have hzero : S.ψ = 0 := Subsingleton.elim _ _
   177	  have hnorm := S.ψ_norm
   178	  rw [hzero, norm_zero] at hnorm
   179	  exact zero_ne_one hnorm

   183	    [Nonempty (S.ιA × S.ιB)] : PureState (S.ιA × S.ιB) where
   184	  vector := S.ψ
   185	  unit := by

   188	    norm_num

     9	# The directly indexed low-degree game
    10	
    11	The low-degree game used by the Pauli-basis combining argument is needed in
    12	dimension `2 * m + 2`.  The existing conditionally linear game represents a
    13	coordinate index by an equally sized fiber in the scalar field and therefore
    14	requires the dimension to divide the field size.  This file gives the separate
    15	directly indexed variant which samples that index directly.
    16	
    17	The geometric line carrier records the sampled coordinate, and line evaluation
    18	uses an `Option` outcome rather than assigning a value when a point does not
    19	determine one.  The game retains the point, axis-line, and diagonal-line answer
    20	formats and the nine ordered type branches of the original low-degree game.
    21	
    22	The `Transport` modules relate the direct game to the seed-indexed game and to
    23	the low individual degree test: `Transport.Correspondence`
    24	identifies coordinates, answers, and the question law of the two QPBT
    25	presentations; `Transport.SeedFiber` dilates a seed-indexed strategy to a
    26	direct strategy by a correlated residue register, and `Transport.SeedFiberValue`
    27	shows that the dilation preserves the value exactly; `Transport.Questions`
    28	reads LDT lines as canonical direct questions and rebases direct answers;
    29	`Transport.Strategy` reads one coordinate of a projective direct strategy as a
    30	LDT projective strategy, with exact Born-weight formulas for both constructions;
    31	`Transport.Consistency` reexpresses the three single-polynomial LDT consistency
    32	relations in direct coordinates, the first two at a fixed tuple coordinate; and
    33	`Transport.BranchComparison`, `Transport.DiagonalRecursion`, and
    34	`Transport.PassConversion` convert a value bound of the direct game into the
    35	pass hypothesis of the low individual degree theorem for every
    36	coordinate strategy.  `GameValue` supplies the rejection calculus relating the
    37	direct value to the LDT branch weights.

  1890	\begin{remark}[Divisibility obstruction in the application of the classical
  1891		soundness theorem]
  1892		\label{rem:qld-4-7-divisibility}
  1893		Definition~\ref{def:ld-game} defines the classical low individual
  1894		degree game only when its dimension parameter divides $q$: the index
  1895		function $\chi$ of the question distribution
  1896		(Definition~\ref{def:ld-question-distribution}) partitions $\F_q$ into
  1897		classes of equal size, one for each coordinate. The same divisibility
  1898		underlies the line-point distribution over $\F_q^{2m+2}$
  1899		(Definition~\ref{def:line-point-dist} instantiated at dimension
  1900		$2m+2$), and with it the statements of Lemmas~\ref{lem:qld-sublines}
  1901		and~\ref{lem:qld-4-13} and the proofs of all three of
  1902		Lemmas~\ref{lem:qld-sublines}, \ref{lem:qld-4-13}
  1903		and~\ref{lem:qld-4-7}. The condition that $2m+2$ divide $q$ does not
  1904		follow from admissibility of $(q,m,d)$
  1905		(Definition~\ref{def:admissible}), which supplies only that $m$
  1906		divides $q$; indeed the two are jointly satisfiable only in a
  1907		degenerate range. An admissible field size
  1908		(Definition~\ref{def:admissible-size}) is a power of two, so $m$
  1909		dividing $q$ forces $m$ to be a power of two; for $m \ge 2$ the
  1910		integer $m+1$ is odd and exceeds $1$, so $2m+2 = 2(m+1)$ divides no
  1911		power of two, while for $m = 1$ the condition $4 \mid q$ holds for
  1912		every admissible $q$ except $q = 2$. The source proof in
  1913		\cite{Ji2020MIPStar} performs the instantiation at dimension $2m+2$
  1914		without addressing the divisibility. The statements above are
  1915		therefore retained in their source form, and for admissible
  1916		parameters with $m \ge 2$ their proofs, like the source's, are
  1917		blocked at the marked steps, so the conclusions are not established
  1918		for such parameters, here or in the source. A proof covering every
  1919		admissible parameter tuple requires a formulation of the game, of its
  1920		question distribution, and of Theorem~\ref{lem:ld-soundness} that
  1921		applies to dimensions not dividing $q$; the missing step and the
  1922		candidate repairs are analyzed in
  1923		\cite{gap:qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility}.
  1924	\end{remark}

    59	\section{Key theorem forms}
    60	
    61	Throughout, $q = 2^k$ with $k$ odd is an admissible field size, the tuple
    62	$(q,m,d)$ is admissible when moreover $d \ge 1$ and $m \mid q$, and
    63	$\mathrm{ideg}_{d,m}(\F_q)$ denotes the $m$-variate polynomial representatives
    64	over $\F_q$ of individual degree at most $d$.  The comparison involves four
    65	theorem forms.
    66	\begin{enumerate}
    67	  \item \textbf{Source theorem form} (the polynomial-pair measurement).  There
    68	  is a function $\delta_S(\eps,m,d,q) = a(md)^a(\eps^b + q^{-b} + 2^{-bmd})$,
    69	  for universal constants $a > 1$ and $0 < b < 1$, such that for every
    70	  admissible $(q,m,d)$ and every projective strategy for the Pauli basis test
    71	  succeeding with probability at least $1-\eps$, there is a projective
    72	  measurement $\{\hat S_{g_X,g_Z}\}$ with outcomes pairs of polynomials in
    73	  $\mathrm{ideg}_{d,m}(\F_q)$ whose evaluations are $\delta_S$-consistent, on
    74	  average over a uniform point $u \in \F_q^m$ and in both bases
    75	  $W \in \{X,Z\}$, with the corresponding points measurements
    76	  $\{\hat M^{(\mathrm{Point},W),u}_a\}$ of the strategy, together with the
    77	  symmetric counterpart of this relation.
    78	  \item \textbf{Missing instantiation obligation.}  The classical low
    79	  individual degree game with parameter tuple $(q,\, 2m+2,\, d,\, 1)$ is well
    80	  defined, and the combined point and line measurements assembled in the
    81	  analysis constitute a strategy for it of value at least
    82	  $1 - \delta_{\mathrm{combine}}$.  The game's question distribution draws
    83	  its axis and diagonal indices through an index function
    84	  $\chi_{2m+2}\colon \F_q \to \{1,\ldots,2m+2\}$ with classes of equal size
    85	  $q/(2m+2)$, so the game exists only when $2m+2$ divides $q$.
    86	  \item \textbf{Restricted form supported by the present route.}  The source
    87	  theorem form under the additional hypothesis $2m+2 \mid q$.  Among
    88	  admissible tuples this hypothesis holds exactly when $m = 1$ and
    89	  $q \ge 8$; it fails for every admissible tuple with $m \ge 2$ and for
    90	  $(q,m) = (2,1)$.
    91	  \item \textbf{Repaired import form} (recommended target).  Quantum
    92	  soundness of the directly indexed variant of the classical low individual
    93	  degree game over $\F_q^{m'}$, for every dimension $m' \ge 1$ and
    94	  admissible $q$, with no divisibility hypothesis: the question
    95	  distribution samples the axis index, and the diagonal prefix index,
    96	  uniformly from $\{1,\ldots,m'\}$ directly rather than through an index
    97	  function on $\F_q$, and line questions carry the sampled index itself in
    98	  place of the seed $s \in \F_q$; the error is
    99	  $\delta_{\mathrm{ld}}(\eps,q,m',d,k) = a(dm'k)^a(\eps^b + q^{-b} +
   100	  2^{-bm'd})$.  This is a candidate target form, not an established one:
   101	  proving it carries the same two import obligations as the $\chi$-based
   102	  import (Section~\ref{sec:import-obligations}), and deriving the present
   103	  form from it when $m' \mid q$ requires the strategy transport described
   104	  under the candidate repairs below, whose synchronicity step is an open
   105	  obligation.
   106	\end{enumerate}
